about: Hardware twins. If you play a real synth or drum machine, the other jammers hear a software twin from the same family: the twin instrument (the unit's own 'twin' if it names one, else its family's), loaded with the preset for your patch type, with this unit's character settings on top. Twins are family resemblances, not emulations. 'character' values override the patch-type preset; 'types' lists the patch types that suit the unit (first is the default). Add a unit by adding an entry. 'osc' and 'filter' describe the circuit (vco, dco, va, wavetable, sample, fm; ladder, ota, ssm, cem, sem, diode, ms20, steiner, arp, svf, digital, none) and refine the twin ranking: a twin or library instrument that declares matching traits ranks higher. Each family lists candidate twins with a rough match score; a unit's own 'twin' is ranked first. Patch sharing: 'dump' holds a model's request for its current sound (SysEx, edit buffer), the reply's prefix and how many messages it has, or failing that how to send a dump from the front panel; gathered from makers' MIDI documentation and open-source editors, merged by tools/merge_patch_specs.py.

setup: Press GLOBALS once (red LED, top row), press program button 2 (MIDI Channel) and pick 1-16 with the BANK/decrement and TENS/increment buttons.
Still on the top row, press 8 (MIDI SysEx) and choose the port you're plugged into: MID for the 5-pin MIDI sockets, USB for USB. There's no separate on/off.
Press 5 (Param Xmit) and set it to NR, then press 6 (Param Rcv) and set it to NR, so knob moves travel as NRPN.
Press 9 (MIDI Out) and pick the same port (MID or USB) so notes and knob moves leave where the app listens.
Don't use Pgm Dump (GLOBALS bottom row, 8) to share sounds: dumped programs load back into a stored program slot. The app asks for the current sound instead.
